results.title: The Evolution of AI in Clinical Decision Support Systems
results.content: A growing trend is **integration through standards** like HL7 FHIR: many EHR vendors now expose FHIR APIs so that third-party AI CDS apps can securely pull patient data and write back recommendations or alerts GitHub. This is exemplified by Epic’s “App Orchard” marketplace which allows approved AI modules (for sepsis prediction, imaging analysis, etc.) to plug into Epic’s workflow GitHub. In practice, a hospital might deploy an AI sepsis warning system that queries the EHR every few minutes via FHIR, analyzes data with its machine learning model, and if a high risk is detected, posts an alert to the patient’s chart for clinicians to see GitHub. Such integrations require robust interoperability, discussed later.

results.title: Designing digital tools clinicians trust
results.content: As clinical workflows grow more complex, digital health platforms have a unique opportunity to reduce friction and restore focus—by embedding trusted decision support directly into the clinician’s workflow. Imagine the value your platform could provide to your clinicians by embedding trusted clinical guidance directly into the workflow. UpToDate is one of the most widely used clinical decision support resource in the U.S., trusted by clinicians in over 90% of hospitals. Whether supporting asynchronous consults, remote monitoring, or AI-enabled triage, UpToDate adapts to the care setting and enhances the clinician’s ability to make informed decisions. By delivering real-time clinical support within the workflow, platforms can reduce clinician burnout, improve outcomes, and build lasting trust with their users. Clinicians regain time and focus, and digital health platforms become the bridge between trust-worthy evidence in real-time and action. Digital health platforms are increasingly expected to deliver trusted, evidence-based clinical guidance within the solutions that clinicians use daily.
